thread:
Emma: Heads-up: BigBank just pushed back — they want a Console UI to pin models (Dedicated/Private). Sales says it's a gating item for signings.
Raj: We already have model pinning in the API, right? What's missing that makes them ask for UI instead of API docs?
Emma: Correct, API endpoints exist. Their PMs say the admin teams are non-engineers and insist on a one-click Console flow + audit trail.
Sofia: Design read: building a full-screen Console feature is non-trivial. Minimal MVP could be a single list with current pins, a dropdown for version, and a rollout toggle.
Liam: From revenue: three prospects made Console pinning explicit. If we deliver a quick Console path, likely to close.
Olivia: Eng note: Console needs backend support for canary rollouts, role-aware audit logs, and an idempotent rollback endpoint. Ballpark: 3 dev sprints + infra.
Raj: Trying a RICE sketch quickly: Reach=medium (enterprise-only), Impact=high (closing deals), Confidence=0.5, Effort=6 sprint-weeks -> score ~3.3 (relative).
Nora: Classic tradeoff: API-first keeps surface area small and easier to maintain; Console-first reduces friction for non-dev admin users. Which do we prioritize?
Emma: Proposal: hybrid sequencing. Phase 1 = ship improved API docs + sample admin React component in docs + telemetry hooks (1 sprint). Phase 2 = Console MVP behind feature flag (2 sprints) if signal meets threshold.
Sofia: Agree. Design for Phase 1: embed a drop-in React component in our docs site; includes pin form + simple confirm modal. No full Console integration.
Liam: Sales wants a clear threshold. Suggestion: 2 signed POCs is enough to greenlight Console work. CS wants 4 successful deploys.
Olivia: We can instrument 'pin.create' events with user role and customer tier. That's lightweight and gives us role-based uptake. Infra impact minimal.
Raj: Risk: API-first delays deal closures for accounts that explicitly stated UI is required. We should list those accounts and treat as exceptions (fast-track).
Emma: Launch criteria I'm proposing for Phase 1: (1) stable pin API + docs + sample component, (2) telemetry capturing role and org for pin events, (3) runbook for rollback + SLO doc, (4) Console design spec ready.
Nora: Good. Also add a policy to gate Console feature to Dedicated/Private only to avoid confusing hosted customers.
Sofia: Small UX detail: add an undo window (10s) and a confirmation step for global pins to reduce accidental flips.
Liam: Action item for Sales: list top 5 accounts demanding UI and mark if they will accept sample component as interim.
Olivia: Action for Eng: scope runbook and make rollback idempotent; add feature flag behind customer tier.
Raj: Emma, can you finalize a small RICE matrix we can attach to roadmap grooming on Friday?
Emma: Yes. I'll produce a 2-row RICE comparison: API-first + sample UI vs Console-MVP and post it in #roadmap by EOD Friday.
Nora: We'll approve hybrid sequencing if telemetry shows adoption OR if any top-3 accounts refuse interim.
Liam: Sales will coordinate with those accounts and give a binary: accept interim vs require Console. Will update by Wed.
Sofia: I'll drop the low-fi Console flows (3 screens) into Figma for review tomorrow.
Olivia: Dev note: include KMS provenance in audit logs for Private customers. Security flagged that.
Emma: Thanks all. Timeline summary: next sprint = API docs + sample component + telemetry + runbook. Console MVP = following 2 sprints if thresholds met. I'll update the roadmap doc after Friday's RICE pass. cc @Nora @Liam @Olivia
Raj: :+1:
Sofia: 👍
Liam: noted
Olivia: ok
Nora: sounds good
